info.title: Erase.me core API
info.description:
The Erase.me core API. Every call is under `/v1`.

**Sign-in and sessions.** Sign in with `GET /v1/auth/google/start`. The `erase_session` cookie (HttpOnly) identifies the user. Send requests with credentials included.

**CSRF.** Every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE needs the `x-csrf-token` header from `GET /v1/me`, and a browser `Origin` that is the web app.

**Errors.** Failures are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`) with a stable `code`. Branch on `code`, not on the text. The `detail` is a sentence a person can act on and never contains draft text, addresses or tokens.

**Outcomes that are not errors.** Creating draft requests answers 200 with one outcome per company: `created`, `existing`, `use_form` (a web-form company: the draft is for copy and paste), `kept` (the user chose to keep it) or `blocked` (with a `reason`, for example `must_keep` or `no_contact`).

**Wording.** Results are hints from header metadata, never statements of fact. The API makes no promise about what a company does with a request.

**Idempotency.** `POST /v1/requests/{id}/send` needs an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.description: The one callback registered with Google, for both sign-in and inbox connect (told apart by server-side state). Always answers with a redirect to the web app: on success to the app, on failure to `/?auth_error=<reason>` (reasons: `access_denied`, `invalid_state`, `exchange_failed`, `scopes_missing`, `no_refresh_token`, `inbox_limit`, `account_unavailable`) and, after connecting an inbox, `/?inbox=connected`. A successful sign-in sets the `erase_session` cookie.

post.description: Makes a draft request for each company, from a fixed template. Always 200: each company has its own outcome. `created` and `existing` are email requests; `use_form` is a web-form company (the draft is for copy and paste, with `formUrl`); `kept` means the user chose to keep it; `blocked` has a `reason` (`must_keep`, `no_contact`, `company_excluded`, `not_found`...). Nothing is sent and no deletion is promised: a draft is a polite request.

draft.subject: Request to erase my personal data
draft.body:
To the Grievance Officer, Sample Shop

I am writing to ask about personal data that Sample Shop likely holds about me.

My details
Name: Asha Rao
Email address: asha@example.com

What I think you hold
From emails that Sample Shop sent to this address, I think you likely holds an account or purchase record.

My request
I would like to ask Sample Shop to erase the personal data it holds about me. I would be grateful for a written reply within 30 days that tells me:
1. whether the data has been erased;
2. if you keep any of it, what you keep, why, and for how long; and
3. if you need anything from me to confirm who I am, what you need.

If you can, I would also appreciate a short summary of the personal data you hold about me.

[OPEN: statute citation and commencement date pending verification. To verify: Section 12(3) (erasure) and Section 11(1) (summary of data held) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023; rights provisions to commence about 13 May 2027 (18 months from 13 November 2025). Replace this paragraph with the verified wording before approving.]

I am also making this request under any erasure process described in your privacy policy.

I am sending this from the email address above. Please reply to it.

Thank you.
Asha Rao

post.summary: Send an approved request from the user’s Gmail
post.description: Needs an `Idempotency-Key` header: a repeat with the same key returns the first answer and never sends twice. Needs a user approval of the exact current draft (also enforced in the database), a verified contact, a company that is neither must-keep nor kept, and text without ID-like numbers or an [OPEN] placeholder. In development and test the sender is fake and the response says so (`delivery: "fake"`, with a `notice`); real sending stays off until it is explicitly enabled. If Gmail does not confirm, the request is left unsent and the user is told to check the Sent folder: it is never retried automatically (`send_outcome_unknown`).

parameters.description: A client-chosen key, 8 to 128 characters (letters, digits and . _ : -). Reuse the same key to retry the same send.

csrfToken.name: x-csrf-token
csrfToken.description: The `csrfToken` from `GET /v1/me`. Required on every state-changing call.

id.description: The detected-company id. Use it for keep and for creating a request.

company.description: Display name, from the catalog or cleaned from the sender domain

signals.description: The header signals this result is based on

confidence.description: `high` means the company likely holds data about the user; `low` means it may. Never certainty.

mustKeep.description: Needed to keep an account working (for example the account provider). No deletion request is offered.

selfServeUrl.description: The company’s own account-deletion page, shown before a request by email. Never set for a must-keep company.

kept.description: The user chose "keep": no request is offered, and a drafted or approved one is refused at approve and send until cleared

activity.description: A hint from message dates: a receipt or similar lately, or nothing for a long time. Null when neither. A hint, never a decision.

openRequest.description: The request that is not yet closed or bounced, if any

authorizationUrl.description: Send the browser here. It is Google’s consent screen for Gmail read and send access.

outcome.description: `created` and `existing`: an email request. `use_form`: the company takes requests through a web form, so the request holds a draft to copy and `formUrl` says where to paste it. `kept`: the user chose to keep this company, so no request is made. `blocked`: see `reason`.

reason.description: Why a request was not made, when `outcome` is `blocked`

message.description: A sentence for the person: why it was blocked, kept or needs the form. Makes no promise about deletion.

selfServeUrl.description: The company’s own account-deletion page, when it has one

revokedAtGoogle.description: False when Google could not be reached: the inbox is still disconnected here, so no further calls are made

csrfToken.description: Send this in the `x-csrf-token` header on every POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE

code.description: A stable machine-readable code. Branch on this, not on `title` or `detail`.

detail.description: A sentence a person can act on. Never contains draft text, addresses or tokens.

instance.description: The request path, without the query string

requestId.description: The `x-request-id` of this call, for support

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Some codes add fields: `use_form` adds `formUrl` and `selfServeUrl` (see ProblemUseForm), `draft_unsafe` adds `findings` (ProblemDraftUnsafe), `validation_failed` adds `errors` (ProblemValidation).

detail.description: A sentence a person can act on. Never contains draft text, addresses or tokens.

instance.description: The request path, without the query string

requestId.description: The `x-request-id` of this call, for support

findings.description: Kinds of problem found, never the text itself

detail.description: A sentence a person can act on. Never contains draft text, addresses or tokens.

instance.description: The request path, without the query string

requestId.description: The `x-request-id` of this call, for support

formUrl.description: The company’s web form. Copy the draft and submit it there.

selfServeUrl.description: The company’s own account-deletion page, if the catalog has one

detail.description: A sentence a person can act on. Never contains draft text, addresses or tokens.

instance.description: The request path, without the query string

requestId.description: The `x-request-id` of this call, for support

errors.description: Where and which rule failed. Submitted values are never echoed.

contact.description: How the company takes requests. For `web_form` the draft is for copy and paste and cannot be sent by email.

to.description: The verified grievance address, or the form URL for a web-form company. Fixed: it cannot be edited.

hash.description: sha256 (hex) of the recipient, subject and body of a draft, exactly as shown

approved.description: True when the user has approved exactly this version of the draft

payload.description: Codes and counts only: never draft text or addresses

blockers.description: Everything stopping this draft from being approved or sent right now

foundCount.description: Companies shown to the user, not counting hidden or "not mine" ones

errorCode.description: For a failed scan, for example `gmail_quota`, `gmail_auth`, `inbox_disconnected`

delivery.description: `fake` in development and test: nothing left the machine

notice.description: Present when nothing really left the machine
